target_customer: Millennial and tech professional retail investors, later higher net worth clients paired with licensed advisors
problem: Hedge fund style strategies and human advisors required very large minimums. Titan offered managed portfolios from $1,000 at a 1% fee and later full wealth management for tech professionals.
business_model: Percentage of assets under management advisory fee (about 1%)

founders.name: Clayton Gardner
education: Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania (met Percoco there)
founders.background_notes: Began investing as a child per TechCrunch Feb 2021.

founders.name: Max Bernardy
founders.background_notes: Named as third co-founder in a TechCrunch photo caption and in Benzinga coverage; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Robinhood
competitors.what: Commission free stock trading app where users manage their own picks

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage integration, fractional share portfolio management and SEC registered adviser compliance; standard fintech engineering with regulatory overhead.

defensibility.rationale: Registration and client assets create some stickiness, but the 2018 strategy of copying disclosed fund holdings was easy to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not copy the hedge fund style product, and Titan grew 600% in 2020 and raised large rounds in 2021, later pivoting to advisor led service for tech workers.

market_need_then: At YC graduation in August 2018 coverage framed it as a robo hedge fund with $1,000 minimums against roughly $100,000 for traditional managed accounts.

branding.domain_note: Used titanvest.com until it bought the exact titan.com after its 2021 Series A (WHOIS suggests about three months later); price not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, human advisor positioning; 2022 revamp aimed at best platform to build wealth; later tagline wealth manager for tech professionals

branding.community_and_virality: Grew 600% in 2020 with effectively no marketing budget per TechCrunch Feb 2021, implying word of mouth; celebrity and athlete investors.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong growth on little marketing and a premium .com, but the name is shared by many Titan companies, including a UK Titan Wealth group.

pivots.from: Mobile robo hedge fund style app with fractional shares
pivots.to: Advisor led wealth management and alternative assets, later focused on tech professionals
pivots.why: 2022 revamp described as offering alternative asset classes; later positioning toward tech professionals with dedicated advisors; reason not stated by a source opened

outcome_analysis: Titan launched at YC in 2018 with a low minimum managed portfolio, was cash flow positive by 2020, grew 600% with no marketing budget, and raised $12.5M then $58M in 2021 at a reported $450M valuation. The company later moved to advisor led wealth management for tech professionals and reports about $1.2B under management on its site. The 2021 boom helped; since then growth appears slower, and no exit or layoffs were found.
notes: Total raised: the Series A release states $16M after that round and press says $75M after the Series B; recorded rounds sum to about $73M, so about $2M (earlier pre-seed or angel money) is unrecorded, hence partial. Series B valuation of $450M comes from Crunchbase News and Business Wire coverage seen in search summaries. Series A investor list is from search summaries of the press release and Benzinga. Titan is also the name of many other firms (Titan Wealth UK, Titan Capital Management) which were excluded from the outcome search. Seed date and amount are from TechCrunch Feb 2021; seed investors not stated there. Competitor sources are dated 2018-08 per search summaries; their pages were not opened and traction fields are null.
